titolo: Trump Called Putin 'My Friend.' Hours Later, Europe Got a Call
angolo: The 24 hours after the Shenzhen handshake: the warm greeting, the empty declaration, and the angry call to Berlin that left allies and Republicans asking what Trump really got.
descrizione: Trump Called Putin 'My Friend.' Hours Later, Europe Got a Call. After the first-ever Trump-Putin-Xi summit in Shenzhen, a four-point declaration skipped Ukraine and Iran, Republicans and European leaders pushed back, and Politico reported Trump questioned Europe's Ukraine aid in a call from Air Force One. A US official told Politico that account was not accurate. We separate what is confirmed from what is only reported.

scene.testo: A greeting. Then a phone call. Then a storm.
Trump points at Putin. Laughs. Says: "He's my friend."
Hours later, Europe was on the line.
What did Trump reportedly tell Berlin from Air Force One?
And was the summit really worth the backlash?
The meeting lasted around ninety minutes, according to ABC News. NPR reported Trump's talks with Putin lasted 42 minutes.
Shenzhen, China. November 19th, 2026.
Leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers. One room.
Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting: "We are really making history."
Video of the greeting spread quickly, and critics condemned it on social media.
Trump pointed at Putin, laughed, and called him a friend.
He also said, "We've had a great relationship for many years."
ABC News noted Putin has sought this kind of recognition for years.
Analyst Jonathan Eyal of RUSI said Putin "gained credibility and escape from pariah status."
Eyal said Trump "gained a photo opportunity he didn't need."
Back in Washington, the reaction came fast.
Senator Mark Kelly said it emboldens Putin.
Chuck Schumer attacked Trump's conduct at the summit.
But Republicans were not united in one voice.
Senator Rick Scott called Putin a thug.
But he added that he understands Trump is trying to get the war to end.
Before the summit, Senator Thom Tillis had told Semafor he'd rather see a NATO summit.
Senator Cornyn said he hoped Trump wouldn't give away too much.
Senator Steve Daines, by contrast, praised the meeting as historic.
Now to the paper that came out of the room.
The leaders issued a four-point peace declaration.
Point one: reform of the United Nations.
Point two: more oil production and supply.
Point three: the International Criminal Court must not abuse its jurisdiction.
Point four: a nuclear war must never be fought.
Notice what is missing.
No mention of Ukraine in the declaration. No mention of Iran, according to AFP.
The White House had first said Ukraine wouldn't be discussed, per the Kyiv Post.
It named nuclear arms reduction and the war in Iran as priorities.
Then Trump said he wanted to raise Ukraine with both leaders.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Ukraine was not the central topic of the trilateral.
Yet Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov called Ukraine the primary focus of the Trump-Putin talks.
Those two statements describe two different meetings: the trilateral, and the one-on-one.
On Iran, the AP reported no sign that Trump secured help from Xi or Putin.
Now the nuclear point. Is it as strong as it sounds?
The declaration said the leaders agreed a nuclear war "must never be fought."
Analysts and arms control experts say the declaration offers rhetoric but no arms-control plan.
Now back to the call that changed the mood.
Politico reported that Trump called into a coalition meeting in Berlin from Air Force One.
Four European officials told Politico that Trump said Putin was serious about negotiations.
Politico also reported, citing three of its sources, that Trump questioned whether Europe should keep spending billions on Ukraine's military.
The Telegraph reported he stressed countries could save money if the war ended.
But the White House side tells a different story.
An unnamed US official told Politico it was not accurate that he told leaders to end funding.
The official said he repeated his desire to bring the conflict to an end.
Jared Kushner said in Berlin that Trump had dialed into the meeting.
In Berlin, Chancellor Merz didn't hold back about the summit.
He called it a "photo op" and said a "Yalta format cannot bring peace."
He said talks can only be successful with Ukraine and Europe.
Yet he also welcomed the US move to start new talks with Russia.
Merz gave each participant at the meeting a piece of the Berlin Wall.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to stand with Ukraine "for as long as it takes."
Ahead of the meeting, the UK said it was funding two fast attack boats for Ukraine; Kyiv Post says it is working with Norway on them.
Burnham said it is not for the aggressor to set out wide-ranging and unrealistic security demands.
And Putin had his own warning for Europe.
At a press conference, Putin said any Europe-Ukraine military cooperation is a problem for Russia.
That includes any troop deployment to Ukraine, he said.
Putin said Ukraine and Europe are not yet ready to compromise, per ABC.
ABC News wrote the meeting may have reinforced Putin's view that the war is going his way.
Putin gets the photo. Kyiv gets questions.

visivo.testo: Putin gets the photo. Kyiv gets questions.

scene.testo: What about Zelensky? He was in Berlin as all this unfolded.
Zelensky said questions about Ukraine must be decided with Ukraine involved.
Zelensky also said both the US and China can help stop the war.
The Kyiv Post says Moscow had hoped to use the summit to discuss settlements.
Two numbers now matter: the next meeting dates.
Trump said he and Putin would meet again.
Republican senators had already questioned inviting Putin to the G20 in Miami in December.
Trump declined to say if he'd meet Zelensky, according to CNN.
Reuters described the summit as big on rhetoric but producing little in tangible agreements.
Two readings of one summit: history made, or history staged.
The story is still moving. Follow for updates.
